These exercises let you practise the verbs from the *Data Analysis 2* part of the course book: `filter()`, `mutate()`, `summarise()`, and `group_by()`. They all use the same `titanic_df` dataset from the course.

Write your code in the box, then click **Run Code** to see the result and get feedback.

The last two exercises are a bit more of a stretch - come back to them once you're comfortable with the rest.

## Exercise 1: `filter()` with one condition

Filter `titanic_df` to keep only the **female** passengers.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_1
#| setup: true
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yann-ryan/infovis-course/master/titanic_df_full.csv"
download.file(url, "titanic_df.csv")
titanic_df <- read_csv("titanic_df.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_1
titanic_df |> ______
```

::: { .hint exercise="ex_1" }
Use `filter()` with `sex == 'female'`. Remember filter needs a double equals sign to check equality.
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex_1" }
#### Solution

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_1
#| solution: true
titanic_df |> filter(sex == 'female')
```
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_1
#| check: true
gradethis::grade_this({
  pass_if_equal(explanation = "That's it - just the female passengers.")
  fail("Not quite. Check you're using a double equals sign (==), and the exact text 'female'.")
})
```

## Exercise 2: `filter()` with a numeric condition

Filter `titanic_df` to keep only passengers **under 18 years old**.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_2
#| setup: true
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yann-ryan/infovis-course/master/titanic_df_full.csv"
download.file(url, "titanic_df.csv")
titanic_df <- read_csv("titanic_df.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_2
titanic_df |> ______
```

::: { .hint exercise="ex_2" }
Use the `<` comparison on the `age` column.
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex_2" }
#### Solution

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_2
#| solution: true
titanic_df |> filter(age < 18)
```
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_2
#| check: true
gradethis::grade_this({
  pass_if_equal(explanation = "Correct - everyone under 18.")
  fail("Not quite. Double check the comparison and the column you're using.")
})
```

## Exercise 3: combining conditions with `&`

Filter `titanic_df` to keep only passengers who were in **first class AND survived**.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_3
#| setup: true
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yann-ryan/infovis-course/master/titanic_df_full.csv"
download.file(url, "titanic_df.csv")
titanic_df <- read_csv("titanic_df.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_3
titanic_df |> ______
```

::: { .hint exercise="ex_3" }
`pclass == 1` for first class, `survived == 1` for survivors, joined with `&`.
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex_3" }
#### Solution

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_3
#| solution: true
titanic_df |> filter(pclass == 1 & survived == 1)
```
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_3
#| check: true
gradethis::grade_this({
  pass_if_equal(explanation = "That's it - first class survivors.")
  fail("Not quite. You need both conditions to be true at once - check you're using & and the right values.")
})
```

## Exercise 4: combining conditions with `|`

Filter `titanic_df` to keep passengers where **either** the fare was more than 100, **or** they were in first class.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_4
#| setup: true
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yann-ryan/infovis-course/master/titanic_df_full.csv"
download.file(url, "titanic_df.csv")
titanic_df <- read_csv("titanic_df.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_4
titanic_df |> ______
```

::: { .hint exercise="ex_4" }
Use `|` instead of `&` to mean "either condition can be true".
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex_4" }
#### Solution

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_4
#| solution: true
titanic_df |> filter(fare > 100 | pclass == 1)
```
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_4
#| check: true
gradethis::grade_this({
  pass_if_equal(explanation = "Correct - either condition qualifies a row.")
  fail("Not quite. Remember | means 'at least one of these is true', which is different to &.")
})
```

## Exercise 5: `%in%`

Filter `titanic_df` to keep only passengers who embarked at **Cherbourg (C) or Queenstown (Q)**.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_5
#| setup: true
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yann-ryan/infovis-course/master/titanic_df_full.csv"
download.file(url, "titanic_df.csv")
titanic_df <- read_csv("titanic_df.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_5
titanic_df |> ______
```

::: { .hint exercise="ex_5" }
Use `embarked %in% c('C', 'Q')`.
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex_5" }
#### Solution

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_5
#| solution: true
titanic_df |> filter(embarked %in% c('C', 'Q'))
```
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_5
#| check: true
gradethis::grade_this({
  pass_if_equal(explanation = "That's it - Cherbourg and Queenstown passengers.")
  fail("Not quite. Check the two letter codes and that you're using %in% with c().")
})
```

## Exercise 8: `summarise()`

In a single `summarise()`, calculate the average (mean) `age`, calling it `mean_age`, and the maximum `fare`, calling it `max_fare`.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_8
#| setup: true
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yann-ryan/infovis-course/master/titanic_df_full.csv"
download.file(url, "titanic_df.csv")
titanic_df <- read_csv("titanic_df.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_8
titanic_df |> ______
```

::: { .hint exercise="ex_8" }
`summarise(mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE), max_fare = max(fare, na.rm = TRUE))`. The `na.rm = TRUE` matters here, since some ages are missing.
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex_8" }
#### Solution

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_8
#| solution: true
titanic_df |> summarise(mean_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE), max_fare = max(fare, na.rm = TRUE))
```
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_8
#| check: true
gradethis::grade_this({
  pass_if_equal(explanation = "That's it - both summary values, correctly named.")
  fail("Not quite. Check your column names match exactly, and don't forget na.rm = TRUE.")
})
```

## Stretch exercise 9: `group_by()` and `summarise()`

For each passenger class (`pclass`), calculate the total number of passengers (call it `total`) and the average fare paid (call it `avg_fare`).

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_9
#| setup: true
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yann-ryan/infovis-course/master/titanic_df_full.csv"
download.file(url, "titanic_df.csv")
titanic_df <- read_csv("titanic_df.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_9
titanic_df |>
  ______ |>
  ______
```

::: { .hint exercise="ex_9" }
`group_by(pclass)`, then `summarise(total = n(), avg_fare = mean(fare, na.rm = TRUE))`.
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex_9" }
#### Solution

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_9
#| solution: true
titanic_df |>
  group_by(pclass) |>
  summarise(total = n(), avg_fare = mean(fare, na.rm = TRUE))
```
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_9
#| check: true
gradethis::grade_this({
  pass_if_equal(explanation = "Great work - one row per class, with the right totals and averages.")
  fail("Not quite. Check you're grouping by the right column, and that both summary columns are named and calculated correctly.")
})
```

## Stretch exercise 10: `mutate()` with `case_when()`

Create a new column called `status`, with **three** categories based on `age`: `'child'` for under 13, `'teenager'` for 13 up to (but not including) 20, and `'adult'` for 20 and over.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_10
#| setup: true
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yann-ryan/infovis-course/master/titanic_df_full.csv"
download.file(url, "titanic_df.csv")
titanic_df <- read_csv("titanic_df.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_10
titanic_df |> ______
```

::: { .hint exercise="ex_10" }
`case_when()` takes a series of `condition ~ value` pairs, checked in order:

```r
mutate(status = case_when(
  age < 13 ~ "child",
  age < 20 ~ "teenager",
  age >= 20 ~ "adult"
))
```

Because `case_when()` checks each condition in order and stops at the first match, you don't need to repeat `age >= 13` for the teenager row.
:::

::: { .solution exercise="ex_10" }
#### Solution

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_10
#| solution: true
titanic_df |>
  mutate(status = case_when(
    age < 13 ~ "child",
    age < 20 ~ "teenager",
    age >= 20 ~ "adult"
  ))
```
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_10
#| check: true
gradethis::grade_this({
  pass_if_equal(explanation = "Excellent - all three age categories, correctly assigned.")
  fail("Not quite there yet. Check each of the three age boundaries carefully, and the exact spelling of each category.")
})
```
